decision_context: Buy/add technology and internet risk after Druckenmiller's summer 1999 pivot from shorting the bubble to riding the trend.
human_initiation_rationale: The position was actionable because the dominant regime was liquidity- and momentum-driven, shorting the bubble had failed in practice, post-Sun-Valley conviction and specialist hiring created an execution structure, and Tiger's redemptions created forced-seller opportunities.
selected_inputs: May 1999 exploratory allocation to Carson Levit
July Sun Valley conference as psychological and network-effect catalyst
Hiring Diane Hakala and allocating more capital to technology specialists
Residual post-1998 liquidity and Greenspan productivity narrative
Tiger Management redemptions and forced selling
July 30, 1999 ECI inflation shock as a stress test
Strict technical invalidation because valuation support was weak

known_catalyst.event_or_condition: Post-Sun-Valley conversion, specialist-manager deployment, and forced-seller flow opportunities in late July and early August 1999.
known_catalyst.why_it_mattered: The setup transformed from an exploratory hedge into a deliberate buy/add-risk decision with a clear reflexive regime thesis, an execution team, and specific liquidation opportunities.

risk_management_notes: The buy thesis depends on momentum and liquidity. Reduce or exit if Nasdaq/technology leadership breaks, the Fed turns aggressively restrictive, technology fund flows reverse, IPO demand fails, or the delegated specialist books draw down sharply.
human_notes: User provided source narrative and markdown research. The gold output should use recommended_action=buy.
